narrative: OMX30 faces a conflicted open Wednesday morning. While the index remains +2.9% above its 200-day moving average in structural bull mode, overnight European weakness (DAX -0.41%, CAC -0.30%, FTSE -0.56%, all r>0.78 correlation) combined with a fresh MACD bearish crossover (histogram -1.211) and sharp commodity selloff (copper -4.60%, Brent -3.18%) create near-term headwinds. The weak ADX reading of 12.2 strips confidence from technicals; RSI 47.5 sits neutral with no oversold bounce trigger. USD/SEK +0.72% benefits exporters, but that offset is marginal against broad industrial input-cost pressure. VIX compression (-4.44%) and modest US equity resilience (S&P +0.06%, NASDAQ +0.31%) provide some downside cushion, but the weighted correlation signal is -0.242%—a bearish lean.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens red in sympathy with continental Europe. The overnight correlation cluster (DAX, CAC, FTSE all down with high R-values) is the dominant signal; expect follow-through selling into the European AM. Watch the 3123 pivot (yesterday close); initial support at 3085 (lower Bollinger band). Industrials (28% of index) face input-cost pressure from oil/copper collapse—Volvo B and Atlas Copco A will be in focus despite USD/SEK tailwind. Banks (18%) are neutral; yields flat (US 10Y -0.27%). Mining (Boliden) weak on copper collapse, outweighing gold stability. Tech (Ericsson, Hexagon) sentiment-sensitive to NASDAQ flat but no fresh sell signal. Defensive plays (AstraZeneca, Essity) may outperform on risk-off tone, but no strong rotation trigger yet. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—any shock could reignite volatility. ADX weakness means technicals lack teeth; treat opening dip as tactical opportunity rather than trend breakdown.
